NOTE:  PUBLIC PARTICIPATION INFORMATION
  Pursuant to the Governor's Executive Order N-29-20 and current State and County Public Health Orders,
  City Council Members will be participating via teleconference.

  - City Council meetings are recorded and live-streamed on the City’s website at www.rhe.city and
  available for viewing thereafter, and televised on Cox 33 and Frontier FiOS 38 on Wednesday and Friday
  following the meeting.

  - Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling: (1-669-900-6833) from any phone,
  Meeting ID: 842 0241 9322, Meeting Password: 066081. (Please note you will not have the ability to
  speak using the call-in option from a phone line.)

  - Public correspondence may be emailed to the City Clerk at cityclerk@rollinghillsestatesca.gov. Emails
  received before 5:00 p.m. the night of the Council meeting will be forwarded to the City Council for their
  consideration and included as part of the record.

  - Members of the public may comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes &
  Videos” page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/MeetingAgendas). Once the agenda is published, there
  will be an “eComment” button next to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to
  the City’s SpeakUp page. After you register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda.
  These comments can be seen by the public, will be considered by the Council and become part of the
  record.

  - Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting may join the Zoom meeting by accessing the
  Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App Store),
  by entering the following credentials: Meeting ID: 842 0241 9322, Meeting Password: 066081. Members
  of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the following
  process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at the
  lower portion of your screen. The City Clerk will send you a chat message to identify which item on the
  agenda you would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city.

CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  FEBRUARY 9, 2021

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order
by MAYOR ZUCKERMAN at 7:05 p.m. via teleconference, pursuant to the Governor’s
Executive Order N-29-20 and current State and County Public Health Orders.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Flag salute led by the Pacifica Boy Scouts of America member Hannah Corr accompanied
by Chaperone Nancy Hodgkiss.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman

City Council Members Absent:  None

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Community Services Supervisor Morquecho
  Community Development & PW Director David Wahba
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit
  Interim City Clerk Carrie Gallagher

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

NONE.

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority
consent of the City Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good
cause is shown by a member prior to the roll call vote. (Items removed for individual
consideration will be voted on separately.)

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN requested to pull item 5F from the Consent Calendar for separate
consideration.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF, TO
  APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS 5A-E and G-H AS FOLLOWS BY THE
  FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS BY TITLE ONLY

  APPROVED.

B.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS OF JANUARY 2021 & FEBRUARY 2021

  APPROVED WARRANTS 63589 THROUGH 63646 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $649,776.88 AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 020121 THROUGH
  020321; IN THE AMOUNT OF $107,210.57 FOR A GRAND TOTAL AMOUNT
  OF $756,987.45 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

C.  GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MINUTES OF JANUARY 19, 2021

  RECEIVED AND FILED.
CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
FEBRUARY 9, 2021
 D.  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES OF JANUARY 25, 2021

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

E.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF JANUARY 26, 2021

  REVIEWED AND APPROVED.

G.  PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES OF FEBRUARY 1, 2021

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

H.  GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MINUTES OF FEBRUARY 2, 2021

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

REMOVED FOR INDIVIDUAL CONSIDERATION

F.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF JANUARY 27, 2021

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN requested a Park and Activities briefing by staff.

  Community Services Supervisor Morquecho thanked Council for highlighting the
  Art in the Park program and for allowing her an opportunity to provide an overview.
  She stated that due to COVID-19 impacts on our youth, local residents approached
  City staff requesting outside space be provided to be used as an outlet within the
  community. Local University students have volunteered to develop and implement
  the program which will consist of one hour long sessions to be held on Saturdays
  lasting approximately eight weeks to be held at one of the local parks with a goal to
  introduce art projects to youth as well as to provide physical health and wellness
  activities. She added that all current LA County health standards for day camps will
  be required as well as live scan and background checks for camp counselors prior to
  program commencement. She added that as a safety precaution, only a limited
  number of participants would be accepted and that proper social distancing would be
  adhered to. The eight week program would be free to participants however an
  anticipated $40.00 material fee would be required, she added that the City would
  administer the registration process and work directly with the instructors.

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN inquired on the age range of attendees.

  Community Services Supervisor Morquecho noted they were in the process of
  working out the details however they were looking at an age range consisting of five
  to 12 year olds.

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN asked that City Council be kept informed of details.

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHMITZ, TO APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEM 5F

  RECEIVED AND FILED SO ORDERED BY MAYOR ZUCKERMAN

6.  PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

NONE.

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

NONE

8.  NEW BUSINESS

NONE

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
FEBRUARY 9, 2021
 9.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  CARES ACT FUNDING REPORT

Administrative Analyst Slawson provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA referred to the staff report and noted the compelling and
noteworthiness of information provided in graph format. She suggested sharing by way of
social media, information regarding the Cities use of 60% of its funding sources to support non-
profits and local businesses

City Manager Grammer supported the suggestion and added that he would insure that the
funding information be added to the City website and shared on social media.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF inquired regarding costs to the City relating to unemployment
benefits and stated that layoffs to City staff had not been necessary.

Assistant City Manager Davis noted an increase in unemployment claims from previous
employees resulting in additional costs and stated that the CARES ACT helped to alleviate
these costs. She added that although no layoffs occurred during this time frame, one position
had been furloughed.

  RECEIVED AND FILED SO ORDERED BY MAYOR ZUCKERMAN

B.  UPDATE ON LOS ANGELES COUNTY SAFER AT HOME ORDER AND STATUS OF
  CITY EVENTS (VERBAL REPORT)

City Manager Grammer provided an update on the Los Angeles County Health Officer Order,
noting there were not a lot of changes to report on since the previous update. He reiterated
that restaurants resumed outdoor dining at limited capacity and that retail stores remain open
also at limited capacity. He added that a decline in COVID-19 cases and hospitalizations are
being reported and public health officials anticipate a decline in the death rate as well. The
vaccination roll out continues slowly and not without challenges specific to shortages of first
doses of the vaccine. Staff has reached out to local health care providers in an attempt to
partner with them once vaccines become more readily available in attempts to make vaccines
more locally accessible to our residents. He added that all avenues are being pursued.

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN inquired on interest from local providers to work directly with the City

City Manager Grammer noted willingness on the part of some providers to partner with the City
however due to the lack of availability, nothing is in place at this time. He included that logistics
are in place and the City is prepared to host a vaccination site once a provider is willing and
able to partner with enough vaccines.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ noted that the meals for students program has resumed
through the Palos Verdes Peninsula Unified School District (PVPUSD) School System, she
added that in class teaching is set to resume on Tuesday February 16 and that Palos Verdes
High School is a designated site for free breakfast and lunch distribution for all students 18 and
under. She noted that this is a very stressful time for students and wishes to keep the dialog
open.

  RECEIVED AND FILED SO ORDERED BY MAYOR ZUCKERMAN

10.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

NONE.

11.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF and Legislative Member of the Palos Verdes (PV) Chamber of
Commerce noted a Virtual Economic Forecast Breakfast event to be held March 19th

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
FEBRUARY 9, 2021
 8:00a.m. – 12:00p.m. scheduled to begin with the installation of the new board, followed by
breakout sessions. She added that there will be limited seating and encouraged those
interested to register early. She shared a report presented by PV School District’s Matthew
Brock on the anticipated opening of grades K-6. She reported on a recent survey conducted
by the library in which the public was asked their thoughts on reopening the library and the
majority of responses were against the reopening at this time. She reported there will be no
immediate changes other than the drive through hours of operation will be extended until 6:00
p.m. at the Peninsula Center and 4:00 p.m. at the Branches. She shared that the Friends of
the Library will hold a virtual gala the weekend of March 19 - March 21 and encouraged those
interested to register early.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA added that the library has resumed booking passport renewal
appointments, adding that the passport program had previously made up more than half of the
library’s revenue.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ asked COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF whether the Council of
Governments (COG), in conjunction with the League and the Chamber had sent out the
Legislative update confirming it to be in February. COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF confirmed this
to be correct.

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN reported attending a recent COG meeting which included a proposal
to hire a regional planner to help cities with matters related to housing. He shared anticipated
per city costs and noted discussions relating to concerns over cost allocation as well as matters
relating to duties and reporting responsibilities of this individual as it related to the expectation
to report to multiple municipalities. He encouraged Council to discuss the item with staff and
requested staff return at the next City Council meeting with direction.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF noted the final COG meeting of the month would be held Thursday
following the next City Council Meeting.

With no objections from Council, City Manager Grammer confirmed that he would agendize
this topic for the next City Council meeting.

MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN inquired of MAYOR ZUCKERMAN whether there was
discussion relating to the Southern California Association of Government (SCAG) funding to
assist with costs related to the proposal to hire a regional planner. He encouraged research by
City staff into SCAG funding options including the use regional grants and believes no direct
cost related to this proposal should be incurred by the individual Cities.

12.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA wished to make Council aware of pending litigation, AB339
in the California Legislature which proposed to preserve digital city council meetings after the
return to open meetings, giving the public the opportunity to stay involved and increase
participation by ease of use.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ suggested in anticipation of the proposed AB339 that an
agenda item be added to the upcoming Policy Session agenda, noting we should prepare for
technical hurdles as it relates to IT infrastructure.

13.  CLOSED SESSION

NONE.

14.  ADJOURNMENT

At 7:49 p.m. MAYOR ZUCKERMAN adjourned the City Council meeting in honor of Steve
Kuykendall, Veteran and longtime member of the Peninsula community who passed away
January 22 and Carolyn Lehr, former City Manager of Rancho Palos Verdes who passed
away on January 31. The meeting was adjourned to the next City Council meeting to be held
on Tuesday, February 23 at 7:00 p.m. for the purpose of a Regular meeting.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

FEBRUARY 9, 2021
 Carrie Gallagher, CMC  Steve Zuckerman
